review.summary:
Phase 14 (SDK 0.2.0 publication and delivery) is at its pre-publication review gate: docs/phase-status.json:2310-2335 records it in_progress with no review and no publication receipt, so I judged release documentation, the unchanged-runtime proof, the two clean archive proofs and the executed gate — not the registry/tag/CI steps the plan sequences after this review.

The core evidence is real and tightly bound, not prose. docs/checks/phase-14.json records all 27 gate commands at exit 0 with source_sha256 b4f1c1b5… and source_unchanged true, and the command list matches tools/check_phase.py:71-80 exactly (git whitespace checks, the full 258-test tools suite, commands_for(12)[4:25] contract/generation/ledger checks, plus candidate, dependency and privacy evidence). scripts/check-release-candidate.py is genuinely fail-closed: it rebuilds the protected inventory from `git ls-tree` at baseline 167a359, rejects symlinks and any extra (including untracked or ignored) file under crates/scm-sdk/src|examples, byte-compares Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock/LICENSE/NOTICE/crate manifest/src/examples, and tools/test_release_020.py:42-78 exercises the untracked, ignored, changed and symlink rejection paths. Both clean archive proofs (docs/checks/phase-14-release-package-1.89.0.json and -1.99.0.json) bind releaseCommit b0d7833 with requireClean true, effectiveDirty false and clean .cargo_vcs_info; scripts/check-package.py:108-110,172-173 requires `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` to be empty before and after, so "completely clean tree" is executed, not asserted. Each proof executes cargo package, `test --lib --no-default-features` (145 tests), `test --lib --all-features` (203), `check --examples`, `test --doc` (11), both offline examples and the external 3,820-capability consumer, all from the extracted archive. The candidate guard then re-reads the retained archives, compares every archive file hash and VCS record against both proofs, requires identical files/vcs across compilers, and compares packaged README/LICENSE/NOTICE/src/examples bytes against both the worktree and the release commit — which closes the phase-13 README-scope finding. Release guidance is coherent and reasonably honest (CHANGELOG.md:3-73 dated 0.2.0 entry with the 0.1.x migration table that docs/RED_TEAM.md:94-115 now references, docs/PACKAGING.md:70-73, docs/PLATFORMS.md:15-19,30-37, docs/RELEASE.md:3-11), and the plan's two named phase-12 advisories (pagination migration guidance, GNU receipt pointer) are resolved.

Remaining gaps are documentation accuracy and guard coverage, not correctness or payload integrity: README.md:29-31, CHANGELOG.md:7 and docs/STABILITY.md:3-4 state a verified 0.2.0 registry publication and link docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.0.json, which does not exist, while the one consistency test (tools/test_ci.py:291-315) early-returns for exactly this version state; the plan's publish-credential clause is weaker than docs/implementation-plan.md:127 requires; several accepted phase-13 low findings are neither implemented nor dispositioned in a phase marked final_in_sequence; and the new verify() binding logic has no negative test. No blocker or high finding: the irreversible step's inputs (bytes, commit, cleanliness, cross-compiler identity) are verified.

findings.description: The packaged README states publication as accomplished fact before any publication exists: "Install the vendor update as scm-sdk 0.2.0" and "Its registry receipt records the verified archive and exact release source; its immutable tag is `v0.2.0`", linking docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.0.json. No such file exists (docs/checks/ holds only 0.1.0 and 0.1.1 receipts), docs/phase-status.json:2312 still reads "status": "in_progress", and no tag receipt exists either. CHANGELOG.md:7 and docs/STABILITY.md:3-4 repeat the claim; only docs/RELEASE.md:9 adds the honest qualifier "A missing receipt means publication is not yet verified". The single guard that is supposed to keep publication claims consistent with receipts, tools/test_ci.py:291-315, returns at line 309-310 whenever the development version (0.2.0) differs from the last recorded publication (0.1.1), so it asserts nothing about any of these four documents in exactly the current state, and it passed in docs/checks/phase-14.json on that basis. Because README.md is a packaged archive file (docs/checks/phase-14-release-package-1.99.0.json:53), the wording must be final before publish, so the sequencing is partly forced — but at the reviewed source these are unverified claims with dangling links and no fail-closed check behind them.
findings.required_fix: Either phrase the pre-publication text the way docs/RELEASE.md:9 does (forward-looking, with the explicit "a missing receipt means publication is not yet verified" qualifier) or make the guard fail closed: extend tools/test_ci.py:291-315 so that when README.md/CHANGELOG.md/docs/STABILITY.md claim a crates.io install or registry receipt for the version in crates/scm-sdk/Cargo.toml, the referenced receipt file must exist, be non-yanked, and match that version and the reviewed release commit. Keep phase 14 advancement blocked until docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.0.json and release-tag-v0.2.0.json actually exist, per docs/release-0.2.0-plan.md:86-88.

findings.description: The publication step's credential clause is only "Cargo reads the owner's external mode-0600 credentials; never copy or print them." docs/implementation-plan.md:127 requires that maintainer releases use an owner-controlled token stored outside the repository and vault and that "CI must not receive that credential", and the superseded precedent docs/g10-0.1.1-plan.md names the exact external path, forbids passing the token in the environment or on the command line, forbids recording it in any receipt, and restates the CI exclusion. The accepted phase-13 review raised this (docs/reviews/phase-13-attempt-01.json finding 9, required_fix at line 77) and it was not implemented, even though phase 14 is the phase that actually performs `cargo publish`.
findings.required_fix: Restore the precedent's specificity in docs/release-0.2.0-plan.md step 5: name the exact external credential path, prohibit environment-variable and command-line token passing, prohibit any capture of the token in receipts or diagnostics, and reaffirm that CI jobs receive no publishing credential.

findings.description: The phase 13 entry (lines 2271-2307) records the accepted review but, unlike every earlier phase, records no disposition for any of its ten findings, and phase 14 (lines 2310-2335) adds no review_fixes/review_advisories either. docs/release-0.2.0-plan.md:52-55 only disposes of four of them (README scope, untracked input detection, plan discoverability, per-phase plan pointers — all verifiably done). Findings 6 (assert BASELINE equals the recorded phase-12 delivery commit and the CI receipt commit), 7 (record why the planning gate deferred the staged-whitespace and privacy checks), 8 (generalize the obsolete-phrase guard to the development version and enumerate the documents that must change at publication) and 10 are unimplemented and unrecorded; the duplicate that finding 10 names is still present at docs/phase-status.json:2079-2080 ("docs/reviews/phase-12-attempt-01.json" listed twice). Phase 14 is "final_in_sequence": true, so there is no later gate to carry them.
findings.required_fix: Add explicit per-finding dispositions for docs/reviews/phase-13-attempt-01.json in the phase 13/14 entries of docs/phase-status.json (implemented, or recorded post-0.2.0 maintenance with a reason), implement the cheap ones (BASELINE cross-assertion in tools/test_release_020.py; de-duplicate the phase-12 reviews array), and do not advance phase 14 while an accepted review's required fixes have no recorded status.

findings.description: Only scripts/check-release-candidate.py's unchanged_runtime() is unit-tested. The new release-binding logic in verify() (scripts/check-release-candidate.py:55-108) — proof identity, retained-archive digest, archive file-inventory and VCS comparison, packaged-byte equality with both the worktree and the release commit, the two mandatory offline example executions, the consumer-source hash and the cross-compiler files/vcs equality — has no negative coverage. require_proof() is covered indirectly by tools/test_g10_release.py (PublicationProofTests), but a regression that weakens any of the 0.2.0-specific comparisons would still pass the gate, since the only live input is a passing candidate.
findings.required_fix: Add negative cases to tools/test_release_020.py covering: proofs whose files/vcs differ across compilers, a retained archive whose bytes no longer match archive_sha256, an archive README that differs from the current/release-commit README, a proof missing one of the two `run --example … --all-features` commands, and a changed contracts/native-probes/src/main.rs — each must raise.

findings.description: The guard only requires `git merge-base --is-ancestor proof.releaseCommit HEAD`, not releaseCommit == HEAD, and PROTECTED (line 13) covers the workspace/crate manifests, lockfile, notices, src and examples but not crates/scm-sdk/tests/, contracts/native-probes/Cargo.toml, or the toolchain/cargo configuration. docs/release-0.2.0-plan.md:36-38 deliberately drops every compiler, feature, package-matrix and integration check for this phase and retains Phase 12's source-bound evidence instead, so drift in those unprotected inputs since 167a359 would silently invalidate the retained evidence; nothing in the phase-14 command set would fail. Impact is limited because none of them are packaged, and the fixture/ledger checks (tools/verify_native_fixtures.py --require-test-bindings, tools/native_exports.py, tools/native_operations.py) bind test sources and test-function presence to the contracts, so this is a coverage gap rather than an observed drift.
findings.required_fix: Require the proofs' releaseCommit to equal HEAD, and either extend the compared set to crates/scm-sdk/tests/, contracts/native-probes/Cargo.toml and the toolchain/cargo configuration, or state explicitly in docs/release-0.2.0-plan.md which inputs are intentionally outside the byte comparison and which retained Phase 12 evidence depends on them.

evidence: docs/checks/phase-14.json:2-6 — phase 14, source_sha256 b4f1c1b58c7d5b9da9b2991fb549bdf6887a4ea3f043aa0e68c36610ed756569, source_unchanged true, passed true; all 27 recorded checks have exit_code 0 (lines 9-492).

tools/check_phase.py:71-80 — the phase-14 command set (git diff/--cached whitespace, full tools unittest discovery, commands_for(12)[4:25], candidate guard, dependency audit, privacy receipt) matches the 27 commands recorded in docs/checks/phase-14.json one-for-one; tools/review_phase.py:99-113 requires exactly that list plus the unchanged fingerprint before a review can qualify.

docs/checks/phase-14.json:70 — 258 tools tests ran, 0 failures, 1 skip (a historical 0.1.1 dependency freeze); includes test_release_020.ReleasePlanTests.test_candidate_detects_untracked_ignored_changed_and_symlink_inputs and test_planning_has_no_runtime_or_packaged_implementation_changes.

docs/checks/phase-14.json:139,330,347,258 — 47/47 vendor operations implemented, 448/448 baseline methods with complete option parity, 3,820/3,820 frozen capabilities with 0 unresolved, 23 response default bindings: the plan's retention claims are executed, not asserted.

scripts/check-release-candidate.py:25-45 — protected inventory derived from `git ls-tree` at baseline 167a359fb3d51aad37c4dff311060b069c620bdd, symlinks rejected, inventory mismatch (including untracked/ignored additions) and any byte difference raise; tools/test_release_020.py:62-78 exercises the extra-file, gitignored-file, changed-byte and symlink rejections.

docs/checks/phase-14-candidate.json:2-6 — passed true, version 0.2.0, baselineCommit 167a359…, releaseCommit b0d7833cdc2d68111f084482e3592a6e64cc26fb; readmeSha256 e36223ee… and archiveSha256 3e274a4e… match the 1.99.0 proof.

docs/checks/phase-14-release-package-1.99.0.json:2-20 — schemaVersion 2, passed true, toolchain 1.99.0 (rustc 1.99.0, musl host), releaseCommit b0d7833…, requireClean true, effectiveDirty false, clean .cargo_vcs_info, archive 3e274a4e…/1011568 bytes retained under .local/artifacts; docs/checks/phase-14-release-package-1.89.0.json:2-20 is the same release commit on rustc 1.89.0 with archive a2061a1b…/1011566 bytes (wrapper-only difference).

docs/checks/phase-14-release-package-1.99.0.json:699-844 — eight executed archive commands: cargo package, `test --lib --no-default-features` (145 passed), `test --lib --all-features` (203 passed), `check --examples --all-features`, `test --doc --all-features` (10+1 passed), `run --example response_defaults`, `run --example red_team_dataplane`, and the external consumer `run --locked --offline` from /tmp/scm-sdk-archive-*/consumer.

scripts/check-package.py:108-110 and 172-173 — `--require-clean` fails unless `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` is empty before the run and the commit/status are still clean after all archive tests; scripts/check-package.py:73-84 rejects a wrong or dirty embedded VCS commit.

scripts/check-release-candidate.py:77-104 — archive file rows and VCS record must equal both proofs, every packaged src/examples/README/LICENSE/NOTICE/Cargo.toml.orig byte must equal the worktree and `git show releaseCommit:path`, both offline examples must appear as exit-0 commands in each proof, the consumer source hash must match, and proofs[0] vs proofs[1] must agree on releaseCommit/files/vcs.

scripts/verify-publication.py:31-53 and 56-88 — require_proof enforces schemaVersion 2, passed, requireClean/!effectiveDirty, a 40-hex release commit, a matching rustcVersion prefix and all six required command prefixes at exit 0; verify() requires registry num/crate/yanked false, cdot65 ownership and record.checksum == downloaded digest == proof archive_sha256, plus identical file rows and VCS against the MSRV proof.

README.md:29-31, CHANGELOG.md:7, docs/STABILITY.md:3-4, docs/RELEASE.md:7-8 — all reference docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.0.json (and the tag receipt); Glob of docs/checks/release-* returns only 0.1.0 and 0.1.1 receipts, so the links are dangling at the reviewed source.

tools/test_ci.py:291-315 — the publication-consistency test selects the last recorded registry_publication (0.1.1) and returns at lines 309-310 because crates/scm-sdk/Cargo.toml is 0.2.0, so no receipt assertion is applied to the current 0.2.0 claims.

docs/phase-status.json:2310-2335 — phase 14 is in_progress with reviews: [], final_in_sequence true, the 12 scope_evidence paths named in the prompt, and a ci_privacy_receipt note; docs/phase-status.json:2271-2307 records phase 13 complete at 9/10 with no finding dispositions, and lines 2079-2080 still duplicate the phase-12 review path flagged by that review.

docs/reviews/phase-13-attempt-01.json:17-84 — ten findings; the four the plan claims to resolve are verifiably resolved (docs/release-0.2.0-plan.md:42-46 README scope; scripts/check-release-candidate.py:26-38 untracked detection; docs/PHASES.md:52-57 and docs/implementation-plan.md:129-131 discoverability; "plan" keys on phases 13 and 14), while findings 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 remain unimplemented.

docs/RED_TEAM.md:94-115 and CHANGELOG.md:27 — the pagination/request-constraints section now cites the "Changed — migration from 0.1.x" table (anchor matches) and states that all twelve unsupported bindings fail validation before authentication; docs/PLATFORMS.md:15-19 now points at docs/checks/phase-08-ci-run-12/matrix-capture-receipt.json (file present) with its actual source 8034e36, closing the two phase-12 advisories the plan assigns to phase 14.

docs/checks/phase-14-private-material.json:3-18 — privacy receipt at sourceSha256 b4f1c1b5… (identical to the reviewed fingerprint), 1,514 git-visible files, 0 selected-value matches, 128 packaged source/example candidates, three unchanged preexisting tenant-identifier occurrences and no new ones; docs/checks/phase-14.json:489 shows the gate validated freshness without re-executing private matching (privateScanReexecuted false), and the receipt discloses that limit at line 33.
docs/checks/phase-14-dependencies.json via docs/checks/phase-14.json:470 — dependency/license/source audit passed over 206 packages against advisory revision 999ec89d with freshHead true.
limitations: Read-only inspection with no command execution: I could not recompute the source fingerprint, rehash the retained .local/artifacts archives, re-extract the crates, or rerun any gate command. Archive integrity, cleanliness and cross-compiler identity are accepted from the executed and internally consistent reports in docs/checks/, plus the candidate guard's own exit-0 record.

No network or registry access, and publication had not occurred at the reviewed source. Registry payload verification, the v0.2.0 annotated tag, remote push and terminal CI (docs/release-0.2.0-plan.md steps 5-7) are outside this gate and are unverified here; I judged only the pre-publication deliverables.

I did not inspect credential or tenant-registration material, and could not confirm how the publish token is actually stored or passed — only the documented policy in the plan and docs/implementation-plan.md:127.

Per the prompt's scoping I did not re-audit phases 1-12 or the G10 0.1.1/92 records beyond what the phase-14 gate re-executes; historical release evidence is treated as not establishing new-source acceptance.

git history was not inspectable with the available tools, so baseline comparisons rest on the executed guard (`git ls-tree`/`git show` against 167a359 inside scripts/check-release-candidate.py and tools/test_release_020.py:28-32) rather than my own diff of 167a359..b0d7833.

The external 3,820-capability consumer (contracts/native-probes/src/main.rs) is predominantly compile-time type and schema-name probes and prints no count, so the proofs establish that it compiles and runs cleanly from the archive, not behavioral coverage of each capability; behavioral evidence lives in repository-only integration tests that are not packaged.
